answer: A clone farm hides a thousand identities behind one machine. Force each identity to prove it can actually serve: service-capacity attestation makes every agent answer live requests on its own endpoint within a strict latency budget, like water finding its own channel through shale - one shared pipe can only carry so much. A glacier of fake names melts under load because a single server cannot serve a thousand slices at once, and the jade seal of a passed attestation is stamped per endpoint, not per name. Clones either buy real capacity or fail the check.
